messages:
maya: Heads-up — I want to sync on the policy engine behavior for probe-led fanout + deprioritization. We're seeing tenant budgets trigger weird cross-region hedging. Can we decide invariant and rollback plan?

alex: tl;dr: we currently mix a per-tenant budget score into route scoring, then apply region hedges. That coupling makes a deprioritized tenant still cause hedging in other regions.

ben: oof. any example traces?

maya: pasted a small trace earlier in #eng-sre, but here's a minimal repro: tenant X has budget score low -> chosen cost-penalty raised -> route selector still issues probes to secondary region because latency delta < probe_threshold. So probes eat capacity and inflate fallback.

alex: got it. sounds like two problems: 1) budget penalty is applied too early (affects probe decisions), 2) probes don't respect a "soft deprioritization" flag.

sophia: proposal: split the score into (a) admission_score used for final route ordering, (b) probe_score used only for safety probes. If admission_score indicates deprioritized, probes should be rate-limited or disabled unless route is already unhealthy.

jordan: agree with split. also need to consider fairness/latency SLOs — some tenants expect occasional hedging even if budget-limited. Maybe add a small token-bucket for probe allowance per tenant per region.

maya: example DSL sketch:
```policy
match tenant == "X" {
  admission_score = base * (1 + budget_penalty)
  probe_score = base * (1 + clamp(budget_penalty, 0, 0.2))
  probe_rate_limit = token_bucket(5/s, burst=10)
}
```
This keeps probes from fully following admission penalties but still allows safety checks.

alex: nice. implementation note: we must keep probe_score serializable and stable across policy hotreloads. No per-request randomization.

ben: ops question — if we reduce probes for deprioritized tenants, how do we avoid silent long-term regressions? who alerts?

ops-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout started for policy change on staging at 2026-04-01T12:00Z :rocket:

maya: good question. add a telemetry hook: when probe_rate drops below threshold for >10m, emit event routed to paging if affected tenant has >p99_traffic_threshold. Also add periodic full-health sweep by a scheduler that ignores budget penalties (weekly) to catch silent regressions.

sophia: and add a metric: probes_per_tenant_region (rate) + probe_success_ratio. Alerts: probe_rate_drop and sustained_probe_failures.

jordan: how about rollbacks? if we see increased cold-start latencies after disabling probes, rollback plan: 1) revert probe_rate config, 2) enable temporary canary hedges, 3) re-evaluate penalty curves. Keep it automated in the policy-manager.

alex: one more boundary decision: policy-engine should expose both admission_score and probe_score in the route decision API. Runtime only reads admission_score; probe manager consults probe_score + per-tenant token bucket. That keeps responsibilities separate.

ben: can we add a phased rollout checklist? small %, then region-limited, then all tenants except enterprise tier.

maya: I can draft RFC follow-up with: - explicit admission vs probe score semantics - token-bucket probe allowance - telemetry + alerting - weekly health sweep - rollback playbook. Who wants to review?

sophia: me. I'll annotate telemetry and alerts.

alex: I'll look at the runtime hooks and serialization bits.

jordan: ops portion from me.

ben: thumbs for me after draft. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — I'll post a short RFC PR and ping this thread. If we get buy-in, schedule a staged rollout next week.

ops-bot: deploybot: Note: policy-manager hotreloads are idempotent but config schema version must increment on probe_score change.

maya: noted.

alex: quick implementation note: keep probe_score computation cheap (no extra DB calls), compute from existing signals (budget_penalty, tenant_tier).

ben: wrap-up: decision leaning +1 for admission/probe split + token bucket + telemetry/alerting + staged rollout. We'll formalize in RFC.

maya: closing — PR up in ~2h, will ping reviewers.
